reason: The text depicts Jehoshaphat establishing judicial systems, appointing judges throughout Judah to ensure fair judgment, and going out among the people to guide them spiritually. He explicitly instructs judges to act without injustice, partiality, or bribery, demonstrating intentional care for the welfare and just treatment of regular people. His reforms—establishing courts in fortified cities, appointing judges in Jerusalem, and instructing them to serve faithfully—show a model of leadership focused on the people's access to justice and proper governance. While the text presents these as positive actions rather than an explicit principle, it clearly exemplifies caring for the welfare of the regular people as the basis of good leadership.
